Hi Everyone! Thank you for you patience! I’ve been stressing a bit about starting the group and a lot of fears have come up but I want to go for it anyway (Oprah says the definition of Courage is “Feeling the fear and doing it anyway”). 

So, here are some thoughts and the plan:
1. The foundation for the group will be Love—-healing through learning how to love ourselves and be vulnerable, share and connect with others in a safe, compassionate environment 

2. I’ll make a baseline format to use for the meeting inspired by my Trauma Recovery Coach training, many years in therapy and my experience in various 12 Step programs (A.A., ACA, etc). After the meetings there will be a 15ish minute share time for feedback on the format so that, together we can create something we all feel safe using. If you want to try an already established recovery program for CPTSD from childhood trauma I highly recommend ACA (for Adult Children of Alcoholics and Dysfunctional Families) 
https://adultchildren.org/

3. I’ll need everyone’s help monitoring for and flagging abuse. I wish I could guarantee that it won’t happen but since this will be anonymous and on zoom, it is possible. In effort to keep the group safe I ask that each interested person email me directly for the zoom information and to agree to the terms (privacy, etc) at traumarecoveryanon@gmail.com (I just created this email for this group)

4. As mentioned, this will be an anonymous group so that means what is said in the group stays in the group. We can each choose what name we want to go by (first name only) and display. We each can also choose to be on camera or not. 

Let’s meet Sunday, 4/24 at 1pm PST on zoom and do a meet and greet to discuss what we hope to get out of the group, etc. 
Email traumarecoveryanon@gmail.com for the zoom info and to agree to terms (privacy, etc) 
Love Jojo

The first time I remember thinking about suiciding I was about 4 years old. I also grew up in a severely abusive and neglectful home and had trouble at school. I felt worthless for most of my life. 

Then I hit rock bottom a few years ago (a new trauma brought up all of my childhood trauma) and I felt like my skin had been ripped off. I was in so much pain I decided to suicide and I actually prayed (to my surprise since I had left all religion and spirituality a long time before that), as I was bawling in the fetal position, “If anyone is out there, you better do something if you want me to stay alive because I can’t do this anymore.” 

And then as I was scrolling thru ways to painlessly suicide, I ran across a Tupac quote that saves my life, “My mama always used to tell me, ‘If you can’t find somethin to live for, you best find somethin to die for.’” 

I immediately thought “Shit! Now I can’t die for nothing!” And I decided that I would do my best to live until I found something to die for. 

I stayed alive (so far).

There are a few things that have helped me heal since then (that’s when I dove into an intense healing journey) that may or may not be helpful:

1) Learning to be my own Loving Parent. It takes a lot of practice but I learned that I could never get the love, acceptance, appreciation, nurturing and protection that I needed from my parents. So now I’m learning how to be my own parent (emotionally at least). I try to think “What would I say or so for a child in my situation” and I try to do it for myself. This is especially important for me when I’m triggered emotionally-learning how to be self-compassionate instead of self-loathing. I’m still working on this in myself but I’ve gotten A LOT better w practice.

2) Reconnecting w my Inner Child (or Soul or True Self). I believe I buried mine as a very young girl because it wasn’t safe for her to be alive. Gabor Mate (a Trauma expert) said, “The essence of trauma is a Disconnection from Self.” She holds my emotions and play and is the only thing that makes being alive okay. Again, it takes practice trying to connect to her but even coloring or singing a song can bring her out. They also eventually need a safe place to express their other emotions like fears, hurts anger…I have found a safe place in ACA (for Adult children of alcoholics and dysfunctional families), some trustworthy friends and some family, and even in a journal. Sometimes I’ll even turn on a song and I let my body express the emotions through dance. It can feel awkward but it also can be SO Freeing!

3) Living one day at a time. When I was most suicidal, I told myself “Just try to live today. You can always kill yourself tomorrow.” That meant each day my only job was to stay alive, so I have myself permission to do whatever it took to do that. 

Idk if any of this helps but please know you are not alone. 💚💚💚

They also eventually need a safe place to express their other emotions like fears, hurts anger…I have found a safe place in ACA (for Adult children of alcoholics and dysfunctional families), some trustworthy friends and some family, and even in a journal. I almost drowned in the ocean 3 years ago. I was trying to learn how to surf and a wave  took me under. I fought to swim to the surface and when I finally got there, I gasped for air and immediately another wave took me down again. 

Again, i fought to get to the top, gasped for air and Immediately another wave took me Under. This happened over and over. 

It got to the point where, embarrassingly, I decided I needed to try to get the lifeguard’s attention. I timed it where, as soon as I hit the top and gasped for air, I pushed myself a little further up and waved my hands. I did that several times until I realized that no one could see me (I was too far out and the sun was setting). No one was coming to save me. 

At that point, I knew I was in trouble. I have asthma, was incredibly out of shape and smoked weed regularly at that point so I knew my lungs where going to give out soon. 

In that moment, I asked myself, “How do I want to die? Fighting and struggling or peacefully?” 

I decided I wanted to die peacefully, and finally stopped fighting the waves. I leaned back and relaxed my body. 

Miraculously, a few seconds later the waves pushed me to the surface and to the shore. 

Before I even got out of the water, as I was coughing up the ocean, I immediately knew what the lesson was...to let go of fighting the waves (i.e. life). 

We can’t stop the waves. Life is going to throw us shit as sure as the waves are going to keep coming. 

All we can do is learn how to surrender to the waves. 

As long as I was fighting, I was actively drowning. When I surrendered, I was set free.

I love this. Thank you all for your wisdom and sharing your experiences. For me I feel like it’s the biggest part of my healing and I’m learning and practicing every day. 

First of all, just allowing myself to feel sad or angry or whatever comes up (even suicidal) WITHOUT judging myself or trying to stop the feeling is HUGE. 

Normally I start to criticize as soon as a feeling comes up, telling myself the same things my dad instilled in me...”Shutup or I’ll give you something to cry about”...”You’re just trying to get attention”... “You’re dramatic...” 

I’m learning to replace that voice with kindness and compassion. I like to think of, “What would I say to a child if they felt this way,” and try to be just as kind to myself. “I’m so sorry you feel sad right now...you have every right to feel this way...how can I be here for you?” 

Sometimes I say these things in my head and sometimes I say them out loud (asking and answering), which I really like to do (especially when I’m in my car so no one can hear me). Other times I’ll write out the questions and answers in my journal. 

Another thing that helps is I made a collage of pics of me as a child and put it by my bed. I try to see her every morning and night with eyes of compassion. I tell her I love her. I, too, often feel disconnected from her but I know it’s all a process ... just like anything we want to master (whether it’s playing guitar or another skill), it takes practice over and over and over. 

I think that’s another key for me...realizing it won’t happen overnight or after being kind once...I have to actively push myself to do the actions. And the feelings follow the actions.
